title: Thigh and glute workout at home
intro: Squats are the best basic exercise to strengthen your thighs and glutes without any equipment. They help with muscle shape and strength, but thigh fat still comes off from the whole body through eating and movement, not from one spot only.
muscles: Quadriceps (front thighs), glutes (bum), hamstrings (back thighs) and core muscles.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out.
Push your hips back as if you're about to sit on a chair.
Go down until your thighs are almost parallel to the floor, or as far as is comfortable.
Chest up, knees following the direction of your toes.
Press your heels into the floor and stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
mistakes: Knees caving inwards. Push your knees slightly out following the direction of your toes.
Heels lifting. Your weight should be on the middle and heels of your feet.
Back rounding. Look forward and keep your chest open.
easier: Chair squat: sit briefly on a chair, then stand back up. You can hold a table for balance.
harder: Hold for 2 seconds at the bottom (pause squat), or do alternating reverse lunges.
dose: 3 sets, 10 to 15 reps. Rest 60 seconds. Do this 2 to 3 times a week. You can add glute bridges, 2 sets of 12 reps, for your glutes.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your knees, hips or back. If you have ongoing knee pain or a past injury, see a doctor or physiotherapist first.

faq.q: Will squats make my thighs bigger?
faq.a: For most people, no. Big muscles need heavy training and eating a surplus for a long time. Bodyweight squats are more about getting stronger and firmer.

faq.q: My knees make a sound when I squat. Is it dangerous?
faq.a: Sounds without pain are usually normal. But if the sound comes with pain or swelling, stop and get professional advice.

faq.q: Can I do squats every day?
faq.a: Yes, in light amounts, for example 10 squats every time you get up from your chair. For full sets, give a rest day between sessions so your muscles can recover.
